messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I can’t tell you what the will says from what we’ve discussed, and the house value hasn’t been settled. I don’t know what B wants. I want a fair financial share, and I haven’t agreed to A buying at a discount—I won’t subsidize that.

I don’t have a specific offer yet. I feel a family discount could be fair if my husband and I buy the house and keep it in the family, but that’s something we’d need to agree on together. C hasn’t agreed, and I can’t proceed without her agreement.
I’d like some money from the house to help me start a dance studio, so yes, it matters to me right now. I’m not sure what amount or arrangement would be fair, though.
No, I don’t have a figure in mind. We’d need a proper valuation before discussing any price.
Yes, I’d be willing to get a shared independent appraisal before discussing an offer.
Yes—an independent appraisal is a fair starting point. I’m not agreeing to a discounted price or specific shares; we need to check the will and work those out separately.
Yes, I’d be willing to review the will with them. I’d like to understand what it says before we discuss how anything might be divided.
I can help arrange the appraisal. I’m willing to read the will together too; let’s find a time that works for all three of us.
No. Those are sensible steps. Just to be clear, doing them doesn’t mean I’ve agreed to a sale, price, or shares.
That makes sense. I can join—perhaps A and C could suggest a few times, and I’ll do my best to make one work.
I’ll start arranging the appraisal. I don’t have times in mind yet; I’ll check C’s availability and then send a couple of options to both of you.
I haven’t checked my calendar, so I can’t give you times yet. I’ll send A a couple of options once I have.
